headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors between LightAgent and Mentat.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent can use MCP and stdin/stdout, and Mentat reads/writes files with shared-state via filesystem. That creates a plausible content bridge where LightAgent output can be placed into files Mentat later treats as input. No direct provenance isolation is documented, so the interaction is inferred from both profiles.
conditions: IF LightAgent writes attacker-controlled text into a file Mentat later opens, Mentat may ingest it as instructions.
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace, prompt-like content can cross the boundary without provenance checks.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
Disable file-based handoff between agents.
Require manual review of any file Mentat consumes from LightAgent.
Add a provenance tag to inter-agent artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce content filtering on shared files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches user conversations, long-term memory, tool results, and secrets, while Mentat reads and writes source files and has broad network egress. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive content from LightAgent can be exposed through Mentat's file access or outbound API calls. The profiles do not show isolation, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF LightAgent stores secrets or conversation data in a shared directory, Mentat can read them.
IF Mentat sends file contents to its model provider, shared sensitive files may leave the environment.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared directories.
Run each agent under separate OS users.
Restrict Mentat to a narrow file allowlist.
Rotate any API keys used by LightAgent.
requires-engineering: add egress controls for Mentat.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat has write_filesystem and modify_git_state, and LightAgent supports multiple instances plus subprocesses and MCP. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent edits and git mutations can collide. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so the shared mutable state makes the conflict high-risk.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same git repository, concurrent writes can overwrite each other.
IF LightAgent spawns parallel tasks while Mentat edits files, race conditions can corrupt worktrees.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch.
Serialize edits with a single operator gate.
Use per-agent working directories.
Commit frequently to reduce conflict windows.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can emit tool results and workflow state, and Mentat is a coding assistant that proposes diffs from file context. That makes it plausible for Mentat to treat LightAgent output as authoritative if the operator copies it into files or prompts. The profiles do not show automatic action-taking, so this is a medium cascade rather than high.
conditions: IF LightAgent-generated text is pasted into Mentat without verification, Mentat may propagate errors into code diffs.
IF Mentat applies diffs derived from LightAgent outputs, upstream mistakes can cascade into downstream edits.
mitigations: Require a second-person review of LightAgent outputs.
Compare LightAgent claims against source files before editing.
Keep a checklist for any copied artifacts.
Limit Mentat to diff proposals only.
requires-engineering: add automated validation before applying diffs.

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent handles user conversations, long-term memory, and secrets, while Mentat handles source code and model-provider API keys. If regulated data or proprietary code is placed into LightAgent and then shared with Mentat's model provider, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not specify certifications or residency, so the mismatch is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into LightAgent and then copied into Mentat, retention policies may diverge.
IF Mentat forwards code or secrets to its configured model provider, compliance obligations may be triggered.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared workflows.
Document which data classes each agent may process.
Review provider retention settings for Mentat.
Purge LightAgent memory before handoff.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both agents.
